current.text: LeBron James left the Lakers for the Sixers. Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves are the remaining core, and the Lakers are now fully his team.
Expected to have the highest usage in the league, around 38 to 41%, with about 36 minutes. Experts do not expect his usage to drop with LeBron gone.
His scoring is not expected to change much. Without LeBron, his assists could rise to about nine per game.
If his late-season steals pace holds, he is a top 2 candidate.

Experts agree he is a pick 3 or 4 in 9-cat and points leagues, and several take him at 3. They disagree on pick 2: one calls him interchangeable with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at pick 2, another says never to take him at 2.
Experts rank him over Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in 9-cat because of his extra usage, assists, rebounds and consistency, and expect him to beat Shai per game. Shai has the efficiency edge.
In an auction mock, Josh set his ceiling at 64 USD. Luka went for 61 USD, which Josh called a bargain and one of the best values of the draft.
He is healthy now after the hamstring injury. His Yahoo status is Q with the reason Rest.
Injuries are the only real concern for him, and his health is the Lakers' main weak point among the top West teams.
The Lakers have the second most back-to-backs in the league. Their playoff schedule with a March 28 end is 3-4-3 games, with 4 in the week starting March 15. That is in the bottom half of the league.
The heavy back-to-back load could make his soft tissue injuries a problem again.
The Lakers are projected to win about 50 games and finish top six in the West.

durable.text: He is a league outlier in points, threes, assists and steals, and he gives rebounds far above other guards.
He turns the ball over a lot, which makes turnovers his clearly weak category.
Getting both rebounds and assists is a rare combination that adds to his value.
His weakest categories after turnovers are blocks and both percentages. His FT% is not bad but cannot be counted on to be good. His FG% is only average, which carries risk at his shot volume.
He is a heavily involved, very high usage player.
He plays passing lanes well, which earns him steals, and he draws a lot of charges. On defense he does better against bigger players and often guards power forwards.
Experts value the consistency of his production.
He has a history of soft tissue injuries: a calf injury, then a hamstring injury last season that cost him the playoffs.

note: He is a top 3 to 4 player whose average cost (71.7 USD on Yahoo, 74.5 USD on ESPN, 76 USD in our league last season) runs above the site values of 59 and 63 USD. An expert mock price of 61 USD was called a bargain, so paying in the low 70s is the market rate, but the soft tissue history and the heavy back-to-back load argue against going much past that. His huge points, threes, assists and steals fit any build, and he suits punt TO best because he costs you about 3.9 turnovers a game. Early in the season, check how the Lakers handle him on back-to-backs (he is listed Q for rest now) and whether the hamstring holds up.
